title: Integrating with Asana's MCP Server
snippet:
This guide walks you through connecting your MCP client to the official Asana MCP server. You'll create an OAuth app in the Asana developer console and use it to authenticate your MCP client.
##
Overview
The Asana V2 MCP server is generally available and uses OAuth for authorization. You'll pre-register your MCP app in the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps), where you can create both standard API apps and MCP apps.
The same registration steps apply to Asana's Command MCP server. Each user needs a Command license. For client-specific setup, see [Using Asana's Command MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-command-mcp-server).
**Important:** Tokens issued for MCP apps only work with the MCP server. This separation follows [MCP security best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/security_best_practices)—if a token is compromised, the blast radius is contained. If you need to make standard Asana API requests, create a separate API app and obtain tokens through the standard OAuth or PAT flow.
---
##
Create your OAuth app
Start by creating an OAuth app in the Asana developer console. This app will handle authentication for your MCP client.
###
Step 1: Create your app
1. Go to the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps) and sign in
2. Click "Create new app"
3. Enter your app name (e.g., "My MCP Client")
4. Select "MCP app" as the app type
5. Click "Create app"
You'll see your app's **Client ID** and **Client secret**. Keep these handy—you'll need them for authentication.

###
Step 2: Configure OAuth settings
1. In the left sidebar, click "OAuth"
2. Add your **Redirect URL**—the callback URL where Asana will send authorization codes
###
Step 3: Configure workspace access
Configure which workspaces can use your app:
1. In the left sidebar, click "Manage distribution"
2. Under "Distribution method," choose one of the following:
- **Specific workspaces:** Select individual workspaces where you want the MCP integration to be usable
- **Any workspace:** Allow the app to be used in any workspace
3. If you selected "Specific workspaces," add the workspace(s) where you want to test
4. Click "Save changes"

Authorization flow
The MCP authorization flow follows the same process as [our existing OAuth authorization flow](https://developers.asana.com/docs/oauth#user-authorization-endpoint), with one key difference: the optional `resource` parameter.

title: MCP Tools Reference
snippet:
The Asana V2 MCP server exposes a set of tools that allow AI assistants to read from and write to your Asana workspace. This page describes the tools, what they do, and when to use them. Availability and tool versions can vary by client and rollout. Use `tools/list` in your connected client to see which tools are available to your session.
> **This list changes over time.** Tools may be added, updated, or deprecated as the tool set evolves. Always use the `tools/list` MCP command in your client to get the current tool schemas. Subscribe to the [developer changelog](https://forum.asana.com/c/forum-en/api/api-changelog/204) for update notifications.
##
**How to use this reference**
Tools are grouped into three categories:
- **Read tools** return data from your workspace without making any changes.
- **Write tools** create, modify, or delete data in your workspace.
- **Interactive tools** display task search results or let you review a task or project before creating it. Availability depends on whether the client supports interactive apps.
**Access and permissions:** MCP apps in Asana do not use permission scopes. When a user authorizes an MCP client, the token automatically requests full access to all available tools. Once authorized, a tool cannot access projects, tasks, or data that the authenticated user does not already have permission to view in Asana.
##
**Read tools**
| Tool | Description | Example prompts |
|---|---|---|
| `search_objects` | Searches tasks, projects, project templates, portfolios, goals, teams, users, tags, custom fields, and AI Teammates by name. Use this first when you do not know an object's GID. Use `resource_type: project_template` to find project templates, `goal` to find goals, `agent` for AI Teammates, or `actor` for humans and AI Teammates together. | "Find the onboarding project template" / "Find the AI Teammate named Triage Bot" |

- **Migrating from V1?** Tool names in V2 no longer use the `asana_` prefix. Task creation and updates use `create_tasks` and `update_tasks`. Many tools that previously required a `workspaceGid` parameter no longer do, because workspace scope is set at authorization time. Review the [V2 changelog post](https://forum.asana.com/t/new-v2-mcp-server-now-generally-available/1122647) for the full list of what was renamed, consolidated, and dropped.

title: developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-mcp-server.md
snippet:
Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows AI assistants and other applications to access the Asana Work Graph. This server provides a way to interact with your Asana workspace through various AI platforms and tools that support MCP.
With this server, you can:
1. Access Asana data from compatible AI applications
2. Create and manage tasks and projects through natural language
3. Generate reports and summaries based on Asana data
4. Analyze project data and get AI-powered insights
Example requests:
1. "Find all my incomplete tasks due this week"
2. "Create a new task in the Marketing project assigned to me"
3. "List all sections in the Product Launch project"
4. "Show me the status of the Q2 Planning project"
## Requirements
1. A compatible MCP client (Streamable HTTP is supported). [There is a partial list of existing clients here!](https://developers.asana.com/docs/mcp-clients)
2. The above MCP client app (or the Asana MCP app, for beta clients) must not be blocked in your workspace via Asana [app management](https://help.asana.com/s/article/app-management-and-integrations?language=en_US). If it is, you will be prompted to send a request for your admin to unblock the app for your domain when trying to authorize.
***
# Connecting to Asana's MCP Server
The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.
This server requires authentication with your Asana account. When connecting, you'll be prompted to authorize the application to access your Asana data.
> 📘 Listing available tools
>
> To view all available tools and their current parameters, use the `tools/list` MCP command within your MCP client. This ensures you always have the most up-to-date list of supported tools.
>
> Subscribe to our [changelog](https://forum.asana.com/c/forum-en/api/api-changelog/204) to stay informed about tool updates and changes.

For MCP-compatible clients:
1. Configure your client to connect to `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`
2. Ensure your client supports OAuth authentication and Streamable HTTP transport
3. Set up the connection according to your client's documentation. You may need to use a client ID and client secret generated by following our [integration guide](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server), if the client doesn't manage this for you.
4. Authenticate with your Asana account when prompted
For developers building MCP integrations, see [Integrating with Asana's MCP Server](https://developers.asana

title: Using Asana's Command MCP Server
snippet:
Asana's Command MCP server lets compatible AI clients work with Command Teamspaces, tickets, and releases. You can search, create, and update tickets, add comments, manage blocking dependencies, and read release status.

1. Each user needs a Command license and access to the Teamspace they want to use.
2. An MCP client that supports OAuth authentication and Streamable HTTP.
3. An Asana MCP app allowed in your workspace through [app management](https://help.asana.com/s/article/app-management-and-integrations?language=en_US).
---
#
Connecting to Asana's Command MCP Server
**Server URL:** `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/command/mcp`
Each user signs in with their own Asana account and authorizes access. To see available tools and their parameters, use your client's `tools/list` request.
##
Create an Asana MCP app
1. Open the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps), select **Create new app**, and choose **MCP app** as the app type.
2. In **OAuth**, add the redirect URL required by your client. It must match exactly.
3. In **Manage distribution**, allow the workspace where the app will be used.
Use the app's **Client ID** and **Client secret** when configuring your client. See [Integrating with Asana's MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server) for app registration details. Use the Command server URL above when connecting.
##
Using with OpenAI
###
ChatGPT plugin
Create one Asana MCP app for a shared custom plugin. Users of that plugin do not need to create their own Asana apps.
1. [Create a custom MCP plugin in ChatGPT](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-mcp-server) with the Command server URL.
2. Select OAuth authentication and enter the Asana app's Client ID and Client secret.
3. Register the plugin's OAuth callback URL in the Asana app and make the plugin available to your workspace.
4. Each user installs the plugin and connects their own Asana account.

Save this server configuration in a local `command-mcp.json` file, replacing `YOUR_CLIENT_ID`:
```
{
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.asana.com/v2/command/mcp",
"oauth": {
"clientId": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
"callbackPort": 8080
}
}
```

title: developers.asana.com/docs/connecting-mcp-clients-to-asanas-v2-server.md
snippet:
The V2 MCP server (`https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`) requires OAuth 2.0 authentication with a registered client ID and client secret. Pre-registration provides better security and gives organizations control over which applications can access their Asana data through app management. This guide shows you how to connect different MCP clients to the V2 server.
## Prerequisites
Before connecting any MCP client to Asana's V2 server, you'll need:
### 1. Create an Asana MCP app
Follow the guide: [Integrating with Asana's MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server)
You'll receive a **client ID** and **client secret** - keep these handy for the next step.

1. Open your shell profile:
```bash
nano ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc for bash
```
2. Add these lines at the bottom (with your credentials substituted in the appropriate place):
```bash
export ASANA_CLIENT_ID="YOUR_CLIENT_ID"
export ASANA_CLIENT_SECRET="YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"
```
3. Save and exit.

When creating your Asana MCP app, set the OAuth redirect URL in the developer console based on which client you're using:
* **Claude Code**: `http://localhost:8080/callback`
* **Cursor**: `cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback`
* **VS Code**:  Both`http://127.0.0.1:33418/`and `https://vscode.dev/redirect`
* **Most other clients** (Windsurf, Kiro, Codex): `http://localhost:3334/oauth/callback`
The redirect URL **must match exactly** between your Asana app settings and your client configuration.
### 4. Install Node.js and npm
Most clients require Node.js and npm to run `mcp-remote`. Download from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org).

You can connect Claude Code to Asana's V2 MCP server natively thanks to its support for OAuth pre-registration.
### 1. Prerequisites
* Claude Code installed ([download](https://code.claude.com))
* An Asana MCP app created ([create one](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps))
* Your Client ID and Client secret from the Asana developer console
### 2. Add Asana MCP server to Claude Code
Open your terminal and run:
```shell
claude mcp add --transport http \
--client-id YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
--client-secret \
--callback-port 8080 \
asana https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp
```
* Replace `YOUR_CLIENT_ID` with your actual Asana Client ID.
* **Wait for the prompt**: After you hit Enter, Claude Code will ask you to enter you OAuth Client Secret.
* Paste your secret there. It will be hidden as you type and stored securely in your local configuration.
